Q: Why do static const declaration within class and inline constexpr definition outside class work together A:

From cppreference.com:

A constexpr specifier used in the first declaration of a function or static data member(since C++17) implies inline. If any declaration of a function or function template has a constexpr specifier, then every declaration must contain that specifier.

The rule (second sentence above) only applies to functions and funtion templates, not to variables. This allows classes like partial_ordering to declare members of their own type (which are incomplete types at the point of the declaration), and upgrade them to constexpr outside the class definition.

Q: VS Code Flake8 linting failed with error KeyError A:

Yeah, this isn’t something you’re doing wrong — it’s a compatibility bug introduced in the VS Code Flake8 extension around 2026.4.0.

What’s actually happening

Flake8 is crashing inside its reporter selection logic:

KeyError: "'%(row)d,%(col)d,%(code).1s,%(code)s:%(text)s'"

That string is being treated as a reporter format name, but in newer versions of the VS Code extension / bundled Flake8, the formatting configuration is being passed incorrectly (or differently escaped) compared to older versions.

So Flake8 tries to look up a “reporter” with that exact string key and fails.

Why downgrading works

Version 2025.2.0 still uses the older expected formatting pipeline, so the misinterpreted formatter string never gets into the reporter lookup step.

That’s why pinning fixes it immediately.

Practical workarounds (until upstream fix lands)

1. Pin Flake8 extension (most reliable)

In VS Code:

  • Extensions → Flake8 → ⚙️ Settings

  • Install specific version:

    ms-python.flake8@2025.2.0

Or disable auto-updates for that extension.

2. Disable Flake8 and use Pylint/Ruff temporarily

If you just need linting working:

  • Switch to Ruff (recommended these days; much faster and actively replacing Flake8 in many setups)

  • Or fallback to Pylint

Ruff especially avoids this whole plugin/reporting layer entirely.

3. Check flake8.format (if you have custom config)

If you have something like in settings:

"flake8.format": "%(row)d,%(col)d,%(code).1s,%(code)s:%(text)s"

Try removing it or reverting to default. That format string is suspicious in the new extension because it’s being misinterpreted as a reporter key instead of a format template.

Bottom line

  • Root cause: regression in VS Code Flake8 extension ≥ 2026.4.0

  • Trigger: broken reporter format handling

  • Fix: waiting for upstream patch

  • Workaround: pin to 2025.2.0 or switch to Ruff

If you want, I can also tell you what changed internally in Flake8’s reporter system that caused this — it’s a pretty subtle API shift and not obvious from the error alone.
